pqac-2bd2246a: Vibrio cholerae RfaH (VcRfaH) shares 35.8% sequence identity with Escherichia coli RfaH (EcRfaH), indicating significant evolutionary divergence. However, VcRfaH exhibits very similar structural properties to EcRfaH. Both proteins display metamorphic behavior where the KOW domain folds as an α-hairpin in the full-length protein and adopts a NusG-type β-barrel conformation when isolated. While VcRfaH has specific stabilizing features like a longer helix and a disulfide bridge, it likely uses a similar fold-switching mechanism for gene expression control as EcRfaH.
From Zuber PK, Daviter T, Heißmann R, Persau U, Schweimer K, and Knauer SH. Structural and thermodynamic analyses of the β-to-α transformation in rfah reveal principles of fold-switching proteins. eLife, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.7554/elife.76630, doi:10.7554/elife.76630.

pqac-489d13a0: The full-length Vibrio cholerae RfaH (VcRfaH) shares a sequence identity of 43.6% with Escherichia coli RfaH (EcRfaH). Structurally, VcRfaH in its autoinhibited state exhibits a secondary structure pattern that perfectly matches that of EcRfaH, suggesting similar tertiary structures for both proteins. A key difference is that VcRfaH contains a disulfide bridge between residues C34 and C102, which covalently tethers the KOW domain to the NGN domain; this feature is absent in EcRfaH. Despite this difference, VcRfaH adopts the same autoinhibited conformation as EcRfaH and its isolated KOW domain forms a five-stranded β-barrel with a Cα rmsd of 1.4 Å compared to isolated EcRfaH-KOW.
From Zuber PK, Daviter T, Heißmann R, Persau U, Schweimer K, and Knauer SH. Structural and thermodynamic analyses of the β-to-α transformation in rfah reveal principles of fold-switching proteins. eLife, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.7554/elife.76630, doi:10.7554/elife.76630.

pqac-0d184fac: Vibrio cholerae RfaH (VcRfaH) shares 35.8% sequence identity with Escherichia coli RfaH (EcRfaH). Despite this divergence, VcRfaH exhibits very similar structural properties and a conserved mechanism of action as EcRfaH. Specifically, the isolated KOW domain of VcRfaH adopts a NusG-type β-barrel conformation, just like EcRfaH-KOW. In the full-length protein context, both proteins fold their KOW domains into an α-hairpin structure. Notable structural differences include VcRfaH having a helix (α3*) that is 1.5 turns longer than in EcRfaH and possessing a disulfide bridge connecting strand β3* and helix α3*, which stabilizes the structure.
From Zuber PK, Daviter T, Heißmann R, Persau U, Schweimer K, and Knauer SH. Structural and thermodynamic analyses of the β-to-α transformation in rfah reveal principles of fold-switching proteins. eLife, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.7554/elife.76630, doi:10.7554/elife.76630.

It mentions VcRfaH (Vibrio cholerae RfaH) in Figure 1 and its supplement, noting that a disulfide bridge forms between C34 and C102 in VcRfaH, which is not explicitly detailed for EcRfaH. The study elucidates structures of both EcRfaH-KOW (PDB-ID: 2LCL) and VcRfaH-KOW (PDB-ID: 6TF4). While the full-length similarity is not directly quantified, the presence of similar structural features like the KOW domain and specific interactions suggests functional and structural conservation between the two species' RfaH proteins.
